frames.narration: 02:55 UTC, everything normal. Every 5 minutes probes in Europe, the US and Tokyo load the home page and run the login journey. Brazilian users load pages with a median LCP of 1.7 s.
03:00 UTC: a CDN edge serving Brazil degrades. Pages there now take about 3 times longer: median LCP rises from 1.7 s to about 5.1 s. Nothing is down, it is slow.
03:05: the probes run again. Their requests use other edges, so every check passes in under a second. There is no probe in Brazil, so the monitoring sees nothing wrong.
Meanwhile each Brazilian browser measures its own page load. 10% of page views are sampled, and about 12% of users block the beacon, so roughly 9 in 100 loads report their LCP.

03:09: the 15-minute window now holds 20 or more Brazil samples and their p75 LCP is above 4 s (it reaches about 7 s), for 3 minutes in a row. RUM alerts, 9 minutes in. About 540 Brazilian page views were already slow.
The fix for the blind spot: add a probe in Brazil. It now fails or times out, and the check is cheap, repeatable and needs no traffic. A 1% sampling RUM would have missed this night entirely.

But a rule that needs 2 of 5 locations to fail would ignore it: only the Brazil probe fails. A rule of any 1 location catches it, and pays for it with about 6 false alarms a day from single-probe blips.
Use both. Probes give a fast, steady alarm and prove login and checkout work at any hour. RUM sizes the damage by country and device with p75. Neither alone covers the other's blind spot.
